title: Feedback Whittle & Winshelf — priority log and microfix roadmap
content:
Purpose:
This note condenses recent customer threads into a compact, execution-friendly format — the "whittle" step: shrink large asks into testable, low-risk microfixes that can be slotted on a "winshelf" for fast delivery. Aim: 8–12 week horizon with clear owners, effort bands, and signal strength so eng + product can pick quick wins without blocking larger programs.

Scope and inputs (last 6 weeks):
- Synth from 42 CS tickets and 6 customer calls (enterprise + mid-market). Top sources: Confluence feedback hub, runtime incident reviews, and field notes from Solutions Eng (see linked artifacts).
- Focus areas surfaced: unpredictable tail latency on short-chat workloads, embedding cost complaints on high-dim vectors, KV-cache invalidation pain when model rollouts occur, and confusing per-route billing spikes.

High-level clusters (ranked by prevalence + escalation frequency):
1) Tail latency spikes for short responses (chat snippets). Signal: 14 unique customer threads, 3 escalations.
2) Billing surprise for embeddings (customers seeing 2–3x cost due to per-batch sizing and hidden retrying). Signal: 10 threads, 2 customers threatened pause.
3) KV cache invalidation semantics during model rollouts — customers report cache thrashing causing cost/latency bump. Signal: 8 threads, affects dedicated/private deployments.
4) Per-route observability gaps — token-level attribution exists but is hard to map to product routes and SDK retries. Signal: 12 threads.

Whittle outcomes: microfix candidates (ranked by impact/effort)
- Microfix A: Short-response fast-path
  - Description: Implement a runtime fast-path that avoids filling large batching queues for requests with expected token <= 16. For these requests, prefer immediate small-batch execution (lower latency, slightly higher unit cost) with a configurable policy flag.
  - Rationale: Many tail complaints happen when short user prompts are pooled behind batching for throughput. Fast-path reduces p99 for short chats by 30–50ms for most workloads.
  - Signal strength: High (14 threads).
  - Estimated effort: Medium (2–3 engineer-weeks to prototype; 1 sprint to stabilize across hosts).
  - Risk: Low — opt-in policy, telemetry guardrails required.
  - Owner suggestion: serving-runtime + eng-sre.

- Microfix B: Embedding-batch-visibility and retry-sleeve
  - Description: Add per-batch metadata to billing/export with explicit attempted_batch_size vs final_sent_size + mark retries. Provide a simple UI/CSV export for customers showing batch-level cost drivers. Also add a client-side retry-sleeve that avoids duplicate billing for transient 5xx within 200ms window.
  - Rationale: Much of the surprise comes from opaque batching behavior + retries. Visibility reduces trust issues; the retry-sleeve cuts a common cost vector.
  - Signal strength: Medium (10 threads).
  - Estimated effort: Low–Medium (1–2 engineer-weeks server + 1 week UI/analytics).
  - Risk: Medium — billing product involvement needed; compliance review for billing changes.
  - Owner suggestion: product-hosted-api + finance-eng.

- Microfix C: KV-rollout-lease and soft-warm cache policy
  - Description: When rolling model versions, instead of immediate global invalidation, apply a lease window (e.g., 30–120s) and soft-warm new nodes with prioritized prefix rehydration for high-traffic customers. Expose a rollout toggle to Dedicated/Private admins.
  - Rationale: Customers report cache thrash when model variants shuffle. A short lease reduces cache churn and avoids an immediate hit to latency/cost.
  - Signal strength: Medium (8 threads).
  - Estimated effort: Medium (3 engineer-weeks; requires rollout orchestration code + metrics).
  - Risk: Low — needs careful correctness testing for stale prefix edge cases.
  - Owner suggestion: serving-runtime + private-deployments.

- Microfix D: Route-mapping observability shim
  - Description: Lightweight agent that stamps inbound requests (route id, API key tag, client sdk id) and surfaces an aggregated per-route latency/cost dashboard slice with a CSV export for audit. Not a full redesign; quick shim to join token-level metrics to route metadata.
  - Rationale: Reduces troubleshooting time for customers and CS by providing a quick crosswalk.
  - Signal strength: Medium (12 threads).
  - Estimated effort: Low (2 engineer-weeks + 1 week dashboard work).
  - Risk: Low — privacy review for token-level joins.
  - Owner suggestion: observability + product-hosted-api.

Winshelf prioritization matrix (proposed):
- Priority A (ship in 4–8 weeks): Microfix A (fast-path), Microfix B (billing export & retry sleeve)
- Priority B (8–12 weeks): Microfix D (route mapping shim)
- Priority C (12+ weeks): Microfix C (KV rollout lease) — requires deeper integration with rollout orchestration

Customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We see random 200ms jumps on quick replies — it's killing our UX for chat completions that are 2–4 tokens." — Large fintech customer
- "Embedding bills doubled last month; our bulk job ended up split into small batches and retried a few times. We don't know why." — Start-up ML team

Open questions and adoption guards:
- Should fast-path be opt-in per-API-key or global with server-side automatic heuristics? Recommendation: opt-in initially; track adoption and p99 improvements.
- Billing retry-sleeve semantics need linkage with finance SLAs. Does finance want automated refunds or merely annotations?
- KV-lease window default: 60s is a reasonable starting point; need SRE simulation for worst-case memory retention patterns.
- Observability shim: privacy and retention policy sign-off from security.

Next steps (owner + timeline suggestion):
1) Triaging sync (this doc + quick 30-minute meeting) — Priya to schedule with leads from serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, observability, and finance. Target: 2026-04-15.
2) Triage meeting outcomes: pick top 2 microfixes to staff a focused 2-week spike each (A and B preferred).
3) Deliver spikes to CS + 1 customer pilot each. 2-week spikes -> 4-week pilot -> measure p99/cost delta.
4) If pilot success, full rollout plan and rollout toggle for Dedicated/Private.

Notes to self / quick links for devs in the spike:
- Slack threads: #cs-runtime-threads (refer message ID in linked_artifacts).
- Customer list for pilots: fintech-corp (prod sandbox), searchai (staging).
- Quick telemetry dashboard: internal/metrics/fast-path-p99 (request to obs team).

Appendix: quick signal table (compact)
- Tail latency (short chat): 14 threads | Escalations: 3 | Urgency: High
- Embedding bills: 10 threads | Escalations: 2 | Urgency: High
- Observability gaps: 12 threads | Escalations: 0 | Urgency: Medium
- KV-cache rollouts: 8 threads | Escalations: 1 | Urgency: Medium

If you want, I can convert this into a one-pager for exec/finance summarizing expected cost delta for each microfix and a recommended funding ask for Q2 quickwins.

-- Priya
